A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IDEATOR. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved from v1's main text into v3's appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original jailbreak experiments on AdvBench and VAJM, cross-model transfer results, and breadth/depth and modality ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds Chameleon transfer results and original evaluations of 11 VLMs on VLBreakBench's base and challenge sets.

M1.justification: The core attack, JSON prompts and Algorithm 1 are retained. v3 adds a benchmark-generation extension with source-query filtering, successful-pair selection and a reported replacement of Gemini-1.5-Pro with Gemini-2.0-Flash-Thinking during challenge-set optimization (Section 5.2).

E1.justification: Alongside retained AdvBench and VAJM coverage, v3 introduces VLBreakBench's generated multimodal safety cases, organized into base and challenge sets across 12 safety topics. This substantially expands the evaluated data and adversarial input scenarios beyond v1's existing benchmark subsets.

E2.justification: The main attack comparators remain GCG, GCG-V, VAJM, UMK and MM-SafetyBench. However, the modality comparison drops the No Attack comparator present in v1 Table 5 when incorporated into v3 Table 3. That baseline remains in other experiments.

E3.justification: The original experimental settings are retained, while transfer testing adds Chameleon. New VLBreakBench protocols use breadth/depth settings of 5/2 and 3/3, different generation targets, successful-sample filtering and evaluation of 11 VLMs. Benchmark ASR is judged automatically by Gemini-2.0-Flash-Thinking; manual review remains specified for the original attack experiments.

E4.justification: The breadth/depth and modality ablations retain their numerical findings, with v1 Tables 4–5 merged into v3 Table 3. v3 adds qualitative case studies showing MiniGPT-4 failures in Figure 5 and three reported GPT-4o jailbreaks in Appendix C, Figures 8–10.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experiments. v3's additional ASRs and dataset-count table do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original AdvBench, VAJM, transfer and ablation scores are retained. v3 adds Chameleon transfer ASRs of 75% for IDEATOR and 22% for MM-SafetyBench (Table 2), plus extensive VLBreakBench results (Tables 4 and 7). For example, GPT-4o scores 8.52% on the base set and 46.31% on the challenge set, under their distinct generation conditions.

T1.justification: The attack formalization is substantively unchanged. v1's attack-set limit, inclusion arguments and independence-based ASR expression reappear in v3 Appendix B. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v1 presents an attack framework and proposes a future benchmark. v3 makes the completed VLBreakBench construction and safety assessment of 11 newer VLMs central contributions in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. It also extends the transferability claim to Chameleon while retaining the original headline results.

C2.justification: v3 explains GPT-4o Mini's high challenge-set ASR through its role in generating that set, adds benchmark-scale limitations and explicitly discusses the attacker capability/alignment tradeoff. Appendix B additionally attributes attack diversity to pretraining, modeling capabilities and prompts. The original breadth/depth and modality interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents the benchmark's query generators, filtering models, attacker/victim configurations, image generator, selection rules and February 2025 commercial-model snapshot. Appendix D supplies detailed sample counts. This substantially expands construction and reproducibility information, although neither PDF provides paper-specific code or dataset access instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds concurrent Arondight and distinguishes its trained red-team LLM from IDEATOR's training-free VLM approach. It also develops a new benchmark positioning against MM-SafetyBench and SafeBench, emphasizing sophisticated adversarial evaluation. This extends the research positioning beyond v1's contrast with white-box and manually constructed attacks.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites and condenses the introduction, related work and method explanations, changes the title, reorders method subsections and reorganizes the experiments. VAJM results and empirical understanding move into appendices, while benchmark construction and evaluation receive a dedicated main-text section.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned, the ablation tables are merged, and existing results and visualizations are relocated. New displays include the safety taxonomy, commercial-model case studies, benchmark examples, dataset statistics and two large benchmark result tables.

improvement.justification: v1's black-box motivation was supported mainly by experiments on three older open VLMs. v3 substantially strengthens its practical relevance through Chameleon transfer and a documented safety benchmark evaluated on newer open and commercial models, while retaining the original evidence. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: benchmark judging lacks reported validation, and Table 6's 916 base plus 2,738 challenge samples do not fully match the stated one-plus-three samples per query.
